name: Minimally invasive anterolateral approach to the proximal tibia (periprosthetic knee)
corridor: Short incision posterior to Gerdy tubercle for a submuscular plate, stab incisions in the proximal half, and a short distal-third window that retracts the deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels

positioning.text: Position so Gerdy tubercle, the tibial crest, and the distal-third anterolateral tibia can be imaged.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark Gerdy tubercle, the prior TKA incision, and the junction of the third and fourth quarters of the tibia where the anterior tibial vessels and deep peroneal nerve cross.

incision.text: Make about a 5 cm cut starting posterior to Gerdy and running distal and anterior. Use stabs just lateral to the crest in the proximal half. In the distal third use a short incision rather than a stab.

superficial_interval.text: Open fascia from Gerdy distally and release the anterior tibialis-anterior attachment. Weigh a new incision against the prior TKA scar; the skin between them is at risk if the operations are close in time.

deep_interval.text: Elevate tibialis anterior without stripping periosteum and retract it laterally. Distally dissect the tibialis-anterior tendon off bone, preserve paratenon, and retract tendon, deep peroneal nerve, and anterior tibial vessels laterally. Proximal stabs may split anterior-compartment muscle bluntly.

layers.text: Skin, anterior-compartment fascia, tibialis anterior, periosteum, then the lateral tibia.

structures_at_risk.text: The deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels, trapped by a submuscular plate or a percutaneous screw in the distal third, and the skin bridge beside a recent TKA scar are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The distal third of the tibia, where the neurovascular bundle crosses the anterolateral surface, is the danger zone for percutaneous screws.

retraction_hazards.text: Preserve paratenon on the tibialis-anterior tendon in the distal window.

exposure.text: Allows submuscular plating of proximal and mid-tibial periprosthetic fractures with percutaneous distal screws only where the nerve and vessels can be seen or safely avoided.

limitations.text: The anteromedial tibial face is subcutaneous and poorly vascular. A recent TKA scar may forbid a nearby second cut.

indications.text: Used for minimally invasive fixation of proximal and mid-tibial periprosthetic fractures.

closure.text: Close the proximal and distal windows after the plate is seated and the neurovascular bundle is confirmed free.

complications.text: Complications include deep-peroneal or anterior-tibial vessel injury, plate entrapment of those structures, and skin necrosis between a new cut and a recent TKA scar.

procedure_applications.condition: A proximal or mid-tibial periprosthetic fracture is plated submuscularly, balancing a new cut against the prior TKA scar

questions.question: Where does the proximal MIO incision start?
questions.answer: Posterior to Gerdy tubercle, about 5 cm, running distal and anterior.

questions.question: Why is a short distal-third incision used instead of a stab?
questions.answer: To expose and retract the deep peroneal nerve and anterior tibial vessels.

questions.question: What must be balanced against a new incision?
questions.answer: The prior TKA scar and the skin between the two cuts.
